breezeml 0.0.1
  • Reference
  • Changelog

    Apply this tab's state to an in-memory EML object via EMLeditor's set_*() functions. Called from run_generation() AFTER make_eml() succeeds and BEFORE write_eml() - this is the "edit before writing to disk" step that replaces the CLI workflow's separate post-hoc editing pass. Returns the modified EML object, or throws (caller wraps in tryCatch).

    apply_permissions_to_eml.Rd

    set_permissions()'s real signature (as of writing, still in development, not yet merged to EMLeditor main): set_permissions(eml_object, access = c("PUBLIC","RESTRICTED","INTERNAL"), legal_authority_id = NULL, contact_email = NULL, authority_designator = NULL, force = FALSE, NPS = TRUE) For PUBLIC access, legal_authority_id/contact_email/authority_designator must be left NULL (not just empty strings) - they are simply not applicable to a public data package, and passing empty strings instead of NULL could be misinterpreted as actual (blank) values rather than "not applicable".

    apply_permissions_to_eml(my_metadata, state)

    Arguments

    my_metadata

    the in-memory EML object (post make_eml(), pre write_eml())

    state

    the list returned by permissionsServer()'s $data reactive, evaluated (i.e. state <- permissions$data())

    Value

    the EML object with permissions, intellectual rights, and language applied

    Details

    force = TRUE is used on every EMLeditor set_*() call in this app: it suppresses interactive/console-oriented behavior (confirmation prompts, verbose output) that doesn't apply in a non-interactive Shiny server context - there is no console for a prompt to appear in.

    NPS = TRUE is used on every EMLeditor set_*() call that supports it: it triggers EMLeditor::.set_for_by_nps(), which adds standard, always-true NPS attribution metadata to the EML object. This app is exclusively for NPS data packages, so NPS = TRUE is hardcoded rather than exposed as a setting - per current guidance, exposing NPS = FALSE as a toggle may be a future feature, but is not needed now.
